task.description: RELEASE-VALIDATOR (WF-02 Step 5) for REQ-159. Independently re-run scripts/test_parallel.sh yourself (2 consecutive clean runs reported, 2229/2229 each). Then confirm every one of REQ-159's real acceptance_criteria (read docs/requirements.yaml directly) is satisfied by checking the actual code/tests yourself: (1) read_variable returns current value/nil, with integer AND float round-trip proving REQ-150's identity rule is genuinely applied; (2) log emits a structured entry with script identity, instance ID, trace ID all individually asserted; (3) get_instance_state returns state for a valid instance and a structured error (not a raise) for an invalid one; (4) each of the 3 functions has a capability-denial test; (5) the number conversion used is LuaNumberMarshalling per REQ-150's naming, cited by section number, no second rule introduced; (6) integer/float round-trip proves the central rule is applied, not just referenced; (7) no host function in this diff calls Letflow.Repo with a script-supplied prefix -- the moduledoc states the tenant prefix comes from calling engine code; (8) mix test/mix compile --warnings-as-errors pass. This run went through 1 design rework for a real cross-instance authorization gap (get_instance_state originally allowed reading any tenant-owned instance) and separately a test-coverage gap where the fix's actual mechanism (no Repo call at all) wasn't verified, only its return value -- independently spot-check that get_instance_state's current implementation genuinely enforces self-instance-only access with no Repo call on mismatch, not just trust the review chain. Also check docs/status/requirement_status.yaml and docs/requirements.yaml for staleness.

acceptance_criteria_verification: AC1 (read_variable current value/nil): platform_test.exs lines 460-491 -- 'returns the current value for a set variable', 'returns nil for an unset variable', plus a malformed-argument case. Verified against do_read_variable/3 in platform.ex (plain Map.fetch on execution_context.variables, no Repo).

AC2 (log structured entry, 3 correlation fields individually asserted): platform_test.exs lines 750-764 asserts script_identity=, instance_id=, trace_id= individually via ExUnit.CaptureLog, plus message text. do_log/3 sources all three exclusively from execution_context, never script args.

AC3 (get_instance_state valid + structured error, no raise): platform_test.exs lines 557-626 cover a valid own instance (returns status/variables table) and invalid_id/no_execution_context/not_found, all returning {nil, %{reason: ...}} tuples, never a raise. Confirmed in do_get_instance_state/3's 4 clauses -- none raises.

AC4 (capability-denial test per function): read_variable (line 510), get_instance_state (line 716), log (line 871) each assert Lua.RuntimeException with the exact capability_required string from @capability_matrix.

AC5 (LuaNumberMarshalling per REQ-150 naming, cited by section): platform.ex calls LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1 at lines 389 and 451; moduledoc/module doc of lua_number_marshalling.ex cites 'REQ-150 SS3' (owning module/function), 'REQ-150 SS2.1'/'SS2.2' (normative rule). Confirmed req150-lua-number-marshalling.md has SS2.1, SS2.2, SS3 as actual headings -- citation is accurate, no second rule introduced anywhere in platform.ex.

AC6 (integer/float round-trip proves rule applied, not just referenced): platform_test.exs lines 493-508 round-trips int_var=3 and float_var=3.0 through platform.read_variable and asserts math.type returns 'integer'/'float' respectively plus exact values -- proves LuaNumberMarshalling.to_lua/1's identity rule is genuinely exercised, not merely cited in a comment. Same pattern repeated for get_instance_state's variables map (lines 567-575, count=1 integer, ratio=2.5 float).

AC7 (no Repo call with script-supplied prefix): platform.ex has exactly one Repo.get call (fetch_instance_state/3, line 439), always prefix: prefix where prefix is execution_context.prefix, never the script-supplied raw_id/instance_id. platform_test.exs lines 989-1009 is a structural source-grep guard asserting exactly this and refuting 'prefix: raw_id'/'prefix: instance_id' substrings.
AC8 (mix test / mix compile --warnings-as-errors pass): both independently re-run above with real quoted output; 0 failures, 0 warnings.
result.get_instance_state_security_spot_check: Read do_get_instance_state/3 (platform.ex lines 416-436) directly. Clause order confirmed: (1) prefix == nil -> no_execution_context, no Repo reference at all; (2) Ecto.UUID.cast/1 on the argument -- :error -> invalid_id, still no Repo reference; (3) only inside the {:ok, instance_id} branch does 'instance_id == execution_context.instance_id' get checked, and the else branch (mismatch) calls encode_error/2 directly -- fetch_instance_state/3 (the only function in this module that references Repo) is syntactically unreachable from that else branch. Only the true branch calls fetch_instance_state/3, which does Repo.get/3. This is a genuine before-any-Repo-reference check, not merely a return-value coincidence. Independently confirmed via the test file's telemetry-based proof too: 'no Repo.get/3 (no [:letflow, :repo, :query] telemetry event) fires for a same-tenant sibling id' (platform_test.exs lines 677-712) attaches a real :telemetry handler on [:letflow, :repo, :query] and asserts a zero count for a same-tenant sibling id -- this is exactly the mutation-testing gap TEST-DESIGNER's note (lines 664-676) describes closing, and I re-ran this specific test as part of the full suite above (it passed, and by inspection could not pass under the 'always call fetch_instance_state' mutation TEST-DESIGNER describes).
